title: Preference Variety (v0.40.0)
description: BCO (Binary Classifier Optimization) trainer plus a unified preference dispatcher in Soup CLI v0.40.0. Set 'task: preference' + preference_loss to swap DPO/SimPO/ORPO/IPO/BCO without renaming the task. β annealing, ref-model regen, multi-objective preference loss (since v0.77.0 blends naming dpo or ipo train too, not only simpo + orpo). Since v0.72.4, dpo, orpo, simpo and kto also run over a layer-streamed base on a card that cannot hold the model, though the unified dispatcher, ipo and bco are not in the streaming allowlist.

headings.title: Multi-objective preference loss (v0.40.1, blend added in v0.53.11, narrowed in v0.76.0)

blocks.html:
Preference Variety (v0.40.0)

Five preference losses live behind one config knob. Pick a loss without renaming your task, anneal β over training, periodically refresh the frozen reference, and blend dpo, ipo, simpo and orpo terms with a multi-objective surface (since v0.77.0 a blend naming dpo or ipo trains too, with the exceptions below).

On a card that cannot hold the model: since v0.72.4, dpo, orpo, simpo and kto also run over a streamed base, where the frozen reference is that same stream with its adapters switched off rather than a second copy of the weights. Note the unified task: preference dispatcher below, and ipo and bco, are not in the streaming allowlist: name the loss in task directly. See Preference losses over streaming.

Row layout (v0.76.1). The examples below read format: dpo, and since v0.76.1 its converter hands the trainer every row in one layout: all strings, or all message lists with the prompt turns in prompt only. A row that cannot be written that way is dropped at load with a reason that names the field. On v0.76.0 a string prompt beside chosen / rejected message lists that repeat the user turn, the shape of the bundled DPO examples, made task: dpo, ipo, bco and preference fail inside trl after the model had loaded; on v0.76.1 they train. orpo and simpo prepare the same tokens as before. See Data formats.

BCO (Binary Classifier Optimization)

Same input format as DPO; rows are split internally to TRL's BCO unpaired schema ({prompt, completion, label}).

blocks.code:
task: bco
data:
  train: ./data/preferences.jsonl
  format: dpo
training:
  bco_beta: 0.1
  lora: { r: 64, alpha: 16 }
  quantization: 4bit

blocks.html:
bco_beta defaults to 0.1 (gt=0). New soup init --template bco ships in the box.

Unified preference dispatcher

Use task: preference + training.preference_loss to swap losses without touching task. Hyperparameter sweeps over the loss type itself become trivial.

blocks.code:
task: preference
data:
  train: ./data/preferences.jsonl
  format: dpo
training:
  preference_loss: dpo   # or simpo, orpo, ipo, bco

blocks.html:
Legacy task: dpo / task: simpo / etc. remain first-class — the unified surface is additive.

KL-controlled DPO variants

Anneal β over training and periodically refresh the reference model.

blocks.code:
task: dpo   # or task: preference + preference_loss: dpo, or task: ipo
training:
  dpo_beta: 0.1
  dpo_beta_schedule: linear   # linear | cosine | exponential
  dpo_beta_end: 0.01
  dpo_ref_regen_epochs: 2     # every 2 epochs, copy the current LoRA adapter into the frozen ref adapter
  lora: { r: 8, alpha: 16 }

blocks.html:
Both controls are gated to DPO-family tasks (dpo, ipo, or preference with preference_loss in {dpo, ipo}). Transformers backend only.

The BetaScheduleCallback resolves total_steps lazily in on_train_begin so the schedule sees the real state.max_steps populated by HF Trainer. Epoch-0 regen is suppressed (avoids copying the untrained student).

Reference regeneration needs LoRA. Under LoRA, TRL keeps a frozen ref adapter beside the trainable one and no separate reference model. Since v0.76.0, dpo_ref_regen_epochs: N copies the active .default. adapter's weights into the .ref. adapter under torch.no_grad() every N epochs, in place (#1345). Full fine-tuning (lora.r: 0) with this key is refused when the config loads: dpo_ref_regen_epochs requires LoRA (lora.r >= 1): full fine-tuning (lora.r: 0) is not supported for DPO-family reference regeneration.

(Since closed in v0.76.0: through v0.75.2 a run that set dpo_ref_regen_epochs or dpo_beta_schedule on dpo, ipo or preference stopped when training started, because the two callbacks were plain classes rather than Hugging Face TrainerCallback subclasses (dpo_beta_schedule with AttributeError: 'BetaScheduleCallback' object has no attribute 'on_epoch_begin', #1229). Neither setting ever took effect, and no finished run exists to re-run. dpo_ref_regen_epochs is wired under LoRA now (#1345, #1636).)

task: dpo with modality: vision now loads a vision-language wrapper checkpoint (AutoModelForImageTextToText plus the model's processor) for text-only preference rows; task: preference with preference_loss: dpo follows it. backend: unsloth does not read modality for DPO and is refused at config load for that combination (#1393).

Multi-objective preference loss (v0.40.1, blend added in v0.53.11, narrowed in v0.76.0)

The schema validates 2–5 entries summing to 1.0 (±1e-6). Single-entry rejected with an actionable message pointing at scalar preference_loss. Mutually exclusive with scalar preference_loss. Rejected on MLX backend.

Since v0.77.0 a blend that names dpo or ipo trains too, whichever loss has the largest weight (#1425, #1785, #1828, by @ybai08), with the exceptions below. The loss with the largest weight is the primary: its trl trainer is the one that is built, and the per-sequence log-probs the terms need are read out of that trainer's own forward pass.

Largest weightWhere the terms come from
dpo or ipotrl's DPOTrainer. The policy log-probs come from its own forward pass and the reference log-probs from its compute_ref_log_probs; upstream: "The reference is run twice per step."
simpo or orpotrl's CPO (SimPO) or ORPO trainer, which return their log-probs from concatenated_forward. A dpo or ipo term needs a reference these trainers do not run, so the blend runs one: the trainer's own forward once more per step, without gradients and with the LoRA adapter switched off. A blend of only simpo and orpo runs no extra forward.
  • Which reference. Under a dpo or ipo primary it is trl's frozen copy of the adapter as it started; under a simpo or orpo primary it is the base with the adapter switched off. For a new LoRA adapter, whose update starts at zero, the two are the same model. They are not with lora.init_strategy: pissa, olora or loftq (or use_olora), which move part of every targeted weight into the adapter, so a dpo or ipo term under a simpo or orpo primary is refused with any of them when the trainer is set up, before the model loads; the config itself loads, so soup train --dry-run does not catch it. Give dpo or ipo the largest weight instead. relora_steps beside a blend that names dpo, ipo or bco is refused at config load whatever the primary (#1891).
  • What a term is. dpo and ipo are the losses preference_loss: dpo and preference_loss: ipo train: DPO's sigmoid loss with training.dpo_beta, and IPO's loss with training.ipo_tau, each log-ratio divided by its response length as trl's IPO loss does. In a blend, simpo and orpo are their preference terms only (the margin or odds-ratio objective), without the likelihood term the standalone preference_loss: simpo and preference_loss: orpo runs carry, so a simpo plus orpo blend is not the same number as either standalone run, and training.cpo_alpha does not affect it. Each term reads its own config field (training.simpo_gamma for SimPO, training.orpo_beta for ORPO) whichever loss is the primary.
  • The same term is not exactly the same number under every primary. The terms are computed on the primary trainer's batch, and the CPO and ORPO batches start with the BOS token where the DPOTrainer's need not, so a dpo term under a simpo primary differs a little from the same term under a dpo primary.
  • Where a blend still stops at the first step. A dpo or ipo term under a simpo or orpo primary in a full fine-tune (lora.r: 0), which has no adapter to switch off, and a trainer that exposes no log-probs to read. The error starts preference_loss_weights: cannot compute <terms>, says why, and names what to change. dpo_beta_schedule and dpo_ref_regen_epochs are refused with a blend when the config loads.
  • What was checked. Upstream's tests train blends on a tiny model and compare the captured log-probs against ones rebuilt independently. No quality or speed result is claimed for any blend.

Through v0.76.1 only a blend that named simpo and orpo alone trained: a blend naming dpo or ipo stopped at the first training step with preference_loss_weights: cannot compute <terms> on this step, because those trainers compute their log-probs inline and publish only means.

  • Evaluation. With val_split set and a simpo or orpo primary, the eval loss is the primary trainer's own loss, not the blend's value, so training and evaluation report different numbers for the same batch. With a dpo or ipo primary, upstream says the eval loss is the blend's value.

bco cannot be combined with a paired loss, and the refusal arrives later than the others: the schema allowlist accepts the name, so the config loads clean and validate_weight_compat raises at trainer setup instead. BCO scores each completion on its own, the paired losses need a chosen-versus-rejected pair, and there is no shared batch shape. Use bco as a scalar preference_loss rather than as an ensemble member.

This surface shipped schema-only in v0.40.0, where training raised an actionable NotImplementedError (the same stub-then-live pattern as v0.27.0 MII / v0.37.0 multipack / v0.38.0 quant menu / v0.39.0 ReLoRA). v0.40.1 replaced that stub with a primary-loss approximation: the highest-weighted loss becomes the trainer and its term is scaled by its weight. v0.53.11 added a per-batch weighted blend on top, but the blend reads the policy log-probs from the batch the trainer receives, and TRL 0.29's trainers do not put them there. (Since closed in v0.76.0: through v0.75.2 the blend then quietly fell back to the primary-loss scaling. {dpo: 0.7, simpo: 0.3} printed Multi-objective preference loss: 0.70·dpo + 0.30·simpo at setup and then trained DPO alone, scaled by 0.7, with nothing in the output saying so. v0.76.0 refuses that instead (#1513) and trains the simpo plus orpo blend described above (#1556). A task: preference run from an earlier version that set preference_loss_weights was a single-loss run.) (Since closed in v0.77.0: blends naming dpo or ipo train too, #1785, #1828.) The NotImplementedError stub is gone.

SimPO caps the prompt since v0.77.0 (#2112, #2116). On the transformers backend TRL 0.29.1's CPO tokenizer cut only the answers, so a long prompt reached the model whole, beyond data.max_length. The prompt is now cut to data.max_length // 2 tokens, keeping its end, and the answers to the room left, as DPO and ORPO do. A prompt longer than data.max_length // 2 tokens is cut even when the whole row would fit, until #1196 lands (upstream's Known Limitation, #1185); a row whose prompt fits in that half and whose whole fits is unchanged.

Re-run this

If you trainedWhat was wrongWhat to do
task: preference with preference_loss_weights, through v0.75.2The blend printed at setup was not the loss that trained. Only the highest-weighted loss trained, scaled by its weight, with nothing saying so (#1425)Re-run as a single loss with training.preference_loss, or as a blend (since v0.77.0 a blend naming dpo or ipo trains too; see the exceptions above)
task: dpo, ipo, or task: preference with dpo or ipo, resumed with --resume, before v0.77.0Upstream: --resume "restored the optimizer and the step counter and trained a freshly initialised adapter: on a 4-step run resumed at step 2, the result was two steps from zero" (#1768, #1797). orpo, simpo, bco and kto were not affectedUpstream: "Re-run any dpo, ipo or grpo training that was resumed from a checkpoint."
task: simpo on a pair where chosen is much longer than rejected and longer than data.max_lengthOn trl 0.29.x the shorter side could end with zero tokens, SimPO's length-normalised log-probability became 0/0, and the adapter went to NaN behind a logged loss of 0.0 (#1208)Check the adapter for NaN or zero tensors and re-run after shortening the data or raising data.max_length. v0.76.0 refuses such a dataset before the first step, naming how many rows, which ones and the data.max_length involved
